# Alessandro N. Garritano

> Microbial ecologist and bioinformatician. Postdoctoral Research Associate at The University of Sydney and Adjunct Fellow at UNSW Sydney. Studies how microbes move carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus through soils and through marine hosts such as deep sea sponges and corals.

ORCID 0000-0002-8159-5178, Wikidata Q139979362. Papers are listed below with their DOIs; the DOI link is the authoritative version.

## Papers

- N. Garritano, A, Hill LJ, Ribeiro B, Damasceno T, Medeiros L, Duarte G, Vilela CLS, Majzoub ME, Allen MA, Nappi J, Peixoto RS, Thomas T (2026). Ammonia oxidation and recalcitrant carbon degradation fuel mixotrophic growth in the symbiont community of a deep-sea sponge. Microbiome 14, 153. Published. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40168-026-02411-y
  Summary: Metagenomics, metatranscriptomics and isotope labelling of the deep sea sponge Calyx sp. Heterotrophs break down tough algal polysaccharides from marine snow while two ammonia oxidising archaea fix carbon worth about a fifth of the sponge’s body carbon a year. The community is mixotrophic.
- Thomas T, N. Garritano, A (2026). Symbiotic Ammonia Oxidation in the Marine Environment. Annual Review of Marine Science 18, 409–427. Published. https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-marine-040824-032008
  Summary: An invited review of ammonia oxidation by microbes living in or on marine animals, from sponges and corals to bivalves and crustaceans. It covers the dominance of Nitrosopumilaceae, the variation in rates between hosts, genomic adaptation to life in a host and the open questions.
- Allen MA, N. Garritano, A, Peixoto RS, Busch K, Slaby B, Hentschel U, Thomas T (2026). The novel, wide-spread sponge-associated phylum Spongivicinota shows metabolic complementarity to its sister-phylum Latescibacterota. ISME Communications 6, ycag317. Published. https://doi.org/10.1093/ismeco/ycag317
  Summary: Seventeen genomes from deep sea sponges define Spongivicinota, a proposed phylum for a widespread clade known until now by placeholder names. Its members live mostly in sponges and corals beside their sister phylum Latescibacterota and specialise in degrading complex peptides.
- Modolon F, N. Garritano, A, Hugenholtz P, Voolstra CR, Keller-Costa T, Costa R, Thomas T, Peixoto RS (2026). Resolving the evolutionary duality of marine symbionts: redefining the genus Endozoicomonas and proposing Neoendozoicomonas gen. nov. ISME Communications 6, ycag123. Published. https://doi.org/10.1093/ismeco/ycag123
  Summary: Phylogenomics across 63 genomes redraws the genera of the Endozoicomonadaceae, symbionts of corals, sponges, molluscs and fishes. Core proteome identity resolved genera best and splits Endozoicomonas into Endozoicomonas sensu stricto and the new genus Neoendozoicomonas.
- Hill LJ, Damasceno T, N. Garritano, A, Modolon F, Medeiros L, Vilela CLS, Duarte G, Thomas T, Peixoto RS (2026). Contrasting microbiomes in deep-sea scleractinian and octocoral species from the South Atlantic Ocean. Sustainable Microbiology 3, qvag048. Published. https://doi.org/10.1093/sumbio/qvag048
  Summary: Amplicon sequencing of stony corals and octocorals from 710 metres in the Campos Basin shows each species carrying a community distinct from the water and sediment around it. The octocoral Candidella imbricata had the most specialised microbiome, dominated by Endozoicomonadaceae.
- Allen MA, N. Garritano, A, Fraser VL, Peixoto RS, Busch K, Slaby B, Hentschel U, Thomas T (2026). Metagenome-assembled genomes and viral sequences from deep-sea sponges. Scientific Data. In press.
- Fu Y, Li J, N. Garritano, A, Wang M, Holmes AJ, Liu SY (2026). Excreta microbiota as an age-associated proxy for gut microbial communities in broiler chickens. Frontiers in Microbiology. In press.
- N. Garritano, A, Modolon F, Warren CR (2026). HiFiTaxa: a reproducible analysis pipeline for full length 16S rRNA gene and ITS amplicon sequencing from PacBio reads. bioRxiv. Under review. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.11.03.763332
  Summary: A Nextflow pipeline that takes raw PacBio HiFi reads for the full length 16S rRNA gene or the fungal ITS region to taxonomy in a single command. It builds versioned references from current GTDB and UNITE releases and runs BLCA, naive Bayes, Emu and EMITS classifiers so their calls can be compared on the same samples. Benchmarked on mock communities and on holdout tests in the preprint.
- N. Garritano, A, Warren C, Holmes A, Liu S, Li J (2026). AmplinkOne: a reproducible and modular R workflow for downstream analysis of microbial marker-gene amplicon sequencing data. Under review.
- Roager L, Schostag M, N. Garritano, A, Gram L, Egan S (2026). Dual transcriptomics reveal commensal interactions between microalgae and phycosphere bacteria. bioRxiv. Under review. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.02.09.704904
  Summary: Dual transcriptomics of two phycosphere bacteria grown with three microalgae. The bacterial transcriptomes changed with the host, and in co culture with the diatom Conticribra weissflogii a Maribacter sp. switched on polysaccharide degradation genes and grew on laminarin alone.
- Modolon F, N. Garritano, A, Hill LJ, Duarte G, Bendia A, De Moura R, Pellizari V, Thomas T, Peixoto RS (2025). Putative promiscuous symbionts in deep-sea corals and crinoids may contribute to nitrogen cycling. Microbiome 13, 234. Published. https://doi.org/10.1186/s40168-025-02229-0
  Summary: Deep sea corals and the crinoids that live on them share the same Endozoicomonadaceae and Nitrosopumilaceae symbionts. A new dominant species, Endozoicomonas promiscua, can reduce nitrate to ammonia, a possible feed for the archaea and a nitrogen cycling link across hosts.
- N. Garritano, A, Zhang Z, Jia Y, Allen MA, Hill LJ, Kuzhiumparambil U, Hinkley C, Raina JB, Peixoto RS, Thomas T (2024). Simple Porifera holobiont reveals complex interactions between the host, an archaeon, a bacterium, and a phage. The ISME Journal 18, wrae197. Published. https://doi.org/10.1093/ismejo/wrae197
  Summary: The glass sponge Aphrocallistes beatrix hosts one archaeon and one bacterium, the simplest sponge holobiont reported. The archaeon runs on sponge ammonia and feeds the bacterium fumarate. Our model suggests that when the virus breaks open archaeal cells, vitamin B12 becomes available to the bacterium. Covered by BBC News.
- Ribeiro B, N. Garritano, A, Raimundo I, Delgadillo-Ordoñez N, Nappi J, Garcias-Bonet N, Villela H, Thomas T, Klautau M, Peixoto RS (2024). Not only for corals: exploring the uptake of beneficial microorganisms for corals by sponges. npj Biofilms and Microbiomes 10, 125. Published. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41522-024-00584-8
  Summary: A four week field trial gave coral probiotics to two sponge species. Related strains were enriched in Stylissa carteri, both microbiomes shifted, and the sponges stayed healthy and kept pumping, so treating nearby corals is unlikely to harm them.
- Hill LJ, Messias CSMA, Vilela CLS, N. Garritano, A, Villela HDM, do Carmo FL, Thomas T, Peixoto RS (2024). Bacteria associated with the in hospite Symbiodiniaceae’s phycosphere. iScience 27, 109531. Published. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.isci.2024.109531
  Summary: A Percoll gradient enriches intact Symbiodiniaceae cells and their attached bacteria from Pocillopora damicornis tissue. Halieaceae, Flavobacteriaceae and Alcanivoraceae associate with the algal cells inside the host, opening the phycosphere within coral tissue to study.
- N. Garritano, A, Majzoub ME, Ribeiro B, Damasceno T, Modolon F, Messias C, Vilela C, Duarte G, Hill L, Peixoto R, Thomas T (2023). Species-specific relationships between deep sea sponges and their symbiotic Nitrosopumilaceae. The ISME Journal 17, 1517–1519. Published. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41396-023-01439-4
  Summary: In three deep sea sponge genera, ammonia oxidising archaea make up at least three quarters of the microbial community, so these holobionts can fix carbon in the dark. Each sponge species carries its own archaeal lineage, which points to vertical transmission. Cited in an international patent application.
- N. Garritano, A, Song W, Thomas T (2022). Carbon fixation pathways across the bacterial and archaeal tree of life. PNAS Nexus 1, pgac226. Published. https://doi.org/10.1093/pnasnexus/pgac226
  Summary: Hidden Markov models screened 52,515 genomes and found carbon fixation pathways in 1,007 of them, including the reverse TCA cycle in phyla where it had not been recognised and a cycle thought to be archaeal in bacteria. Carbon fixation is far more widespread than the textbook picture.
- N. Garritano, A, Faber MO, De Sá LRV, Ferreira-Leitão VS (2018). Palm oil mill effluent (POME) as raw material for biohydrogen and methane production via dark fermentation. Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews 92, 676–684. Published. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2018.04.031
  Summary: A review of palm oil mill effluent as a feedstock for hydrogen and methane by dark fermentation, bringing together the microbiology, the process conditions and the reported yields, and the two stage approach that recovers methane from the spent medium.
- N. Garritano, A, De Sá LRV, Aguieiras ÉCG, Freire DMG, Ferreira-Leitão VS (2017). Efficient biohydrogen production via dark fermentation from hydrolized palm oil mill effluent by non-commercial enzyme preparation. International Journal of Hydrogen Energy 42, 29166–29174. Published. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhydene.2017.10.025
  Summary: Hydrolysing the effluent with an enzyme preparation made in the laboratory from Ricinus communis, in place of a commercial enzyme, raised the hydrogen yield from dark fermentation of this wastewater.
